newsitem.title: UK: IRA admit gun attack on British troops in Derry.
newsitem.headline: IRA admit gun attack on British troops in Derry.

text.p: The IRA claimed responsibility for a shooting attack on British troops in Londonderry on Tuesday in which no-one was injured.

Police said several shots were heard as an army vehicle was passing the Bogside district, an Irish nationalist stronghold. "There are no reports of any hits (on the vehicle) or injuries," a police spokesman said.
The Irish Republican Army, which is opposed to Britain's rule in the province, later admitted the attack in a coded telephone call to a local newspaper.

Soon after the attack security forces sealed off streets in a small housing estate in the Bogside after a van, which they suspected had been used in the incident, was found in the nationalist district.
Thirty families had to leave their homes as police and soldiers, wary of booby traps, investigated the vehicle, security sources said.
The attack was the latest in a series of sporadic incidents that have thrown peace hopes into fresh gloom.

The latest shooting came a year to the day after the launch of multi-party talks that have failed to bridge a wide gulf between the province's Protestant parties, that support British sovereignty, and Catholic politicians who want an all-Ireland state.
